name: How much does a living room renovation cost in Los Angeles for a mid-range home?

mainEntity.name: What is a realistic cost range for a living room or open-concept living-space renovation in Los Angeles if I’m updating flooring, lighting, walls, and finishes but not adding square footage?
mainEntity.text: What is a realistic cost range for a living room or open-concept living-space renovation in Los Angeles if I’m updating flooring, lighting, walls, and finishes but not adding square footage?

acceptedAnswer.text: A realistic budget depends on how much of the room is changing. Cosmetic work like paint, flooring, lighting, trim, and built-ins typically costs far less than projects involving wall removal, rewiring, HVAC changes, or structural reinforcement. In Los Angeles, labor, permit complexity, and finish level can push a living-space renovation well above national averages. Homeowners should budget separately for design, demolition, construction, fixtures, and contingency reserves. A good planning rule is to treat the first estimate as a starting point, then add a cushion for hidden issues such as outdated wiring, uneven floors, or dry rot. If the project is meant to improve resale value, it helps to prioritize visible upgrades and layout improvements that make the room feel larger and brighter without unnecessary custom work. A contractor should provide a line-item estimate so you can compare apples to apples.
acceptedAnswer.description: A mid-range living-space renovation in Los Angeles often ranges from a modest cosmetic update to a major interior refresh, depending on finishes, electrical work, and structural changes. Costs rise quickly when walls move, wiring changes, or custom millwork is added. A detailed scope, not just square footage, drives the final price.
